title: Custom Industrial Ethernet Switch | HT7000 / HT7008 | Hitelecom
metaDescription: HT7000 industrial Ethernet switch customization. HT7008 reference: 8 Gigabit RJ45 ports, 10/100/1000 Mbps auto-negotiation, aluminium housing and -40 to +75 °C operation.
heroValue:
Connect the equipment.
Build the site network.
heroDescription: The Hitelecom HT7000 series brings Gigabit Ethernet connectivity to industrial equipment networks. The pictured HT7008 provides eight RJ45 ports with 10/100/1000 Mbps auto-negotiation, an aluminium-alloy enclosure and an operating temperature range of -40 to +75 °C. Develop the project configuration around the connected devices, cabinet power, installation environment and network requirements.
reviewNotice: HT7008 is the illustrated eight-port reference. The agreed project specification defines the supplied hardware, power arrangement, network functions and applicable verification.

interfaceCards.title: Copper Ethernet connections
interfaceCards.text: Allocate the eight HT7008 ports between equipment connections and any upstream network link. Connect compatible Ethernet endpoints and confirm the negotiated speed of each link.

features.title: Eight-port Gigabit reference
features.text: The illustrated HT7008 provides eight copper Ethernet ports. Build the port schedule around connected equipment, the upstream connection and any required spare capacity.

features.title: 10/100/1000 Mbps auto-negotiation
features.text: Connect compatible Ethernet devices operating at the supported link speeds. Verify the negotiated rate and end-to-end application traffic during commissioning.

features.title: Aluminium-alloy enclosure
features.text: The metal enclosure and external fins provide a practical mechanical format for industrial cabinets. Define mounting, access and thermal clearances for the installation.

features.title: Industrial operating temperature
features.text: The HT7008 reference operates from -40 to +75 °C. Assess the local cabinet temperature, heat sources and cooling as part of the installation design.

features.title: DC supply configuration
features.text: The reference lists 12, 24 and 48 V DC nominal supply values. Specify the input arrangement, allowable voltage tolerance and power-source requirements for the delivered version.

features.title: IEEE 802.3x flow control
features.text: The reference lists IEEE 802.3x flow control. Evaluate its behaviour with the connected devices and traffic profile; link-level flow control does not define application latency.

features.title: Local status visibility
features.text: The product illustration includes a power indicator and port-side indicators. Use the supplied indicator definitions together with endpoint checks to verify connection and operating status.

features.title: A documented custom configuration
features.text: Review port allocation, power, enclosure, network-function requirements and product identification with Hitelecom. Record the agreed design, acceptance criteria and delivery documents before production.

workflow.title: Define the network task
workflow.text: List the Ethernet endpoints, their traffic and the upstream connection. Record available ports, growth allowance, installation location and the project network boundary.

workflow.title: Specify the configuration
workflow.text: Agree the port schedule, DC supply arrangement, mechanical requirements and any requested network functions. Put approved customization and verification scope into the project specification.

workflow.title: Validate the agreed design
workflow.text: Evaluate the agreed sample or configuration with representative equipment and traffic. Verify link negotiation, supply behaviour, cabinet conditions and required recovery procedures against the acceptance criteria.

workflow.title: Document the delivered network
workflow.text: Hand over the port map, power and mounting instructions, approved configuration and test records. Identify upstream equipment and assign responsibility for ongoing network operation.

applicationsIntro: Industrial Ethernet connects equipment at the machine, cabinet and site level. Explore eight application areas and 40 project tasks, then define the actual endpoints, traffic, power and environmental requirements. These are representative integration tasks, not statements of sector certification or a promise that one switch serves every listed device at once.

platformIntro: Place the switch within the project network design. It provides local Ethernet connectivity; the connected endpoints, upstream router or gateway and receiving systems define the wider data path, application services and operating responsibilities.

faqs.q: What is the relationship between HT7000 and HT7008?
faqs.a: HT7000 is the industrial Ethernet switch series. HT7008 is the eight-port model shown on this page. Use its reference configuration to start a project discussion, then confirm the exact supplied version and agreed customization in the ordering specification.

faqs.q: How many equipment links can the eight-port reference provide?
faqs.a: HT7008 has eight RJ45 ports in total. An upstream Ethernet connection also occupies one of these ports. Allocate endpoint links, upstream connections and spares together; do not count an additional unlisted uplink.

faqs.q: Does a Gigabit port guarantee Gigabit application throughput?
faqs.a: 10/100/1000 Mbps describes the supported link speeds. Actual end-to-end performance also depends on the endpoints, cable installation, traffic pattern and other network equipment. Confirm the required application traffic and performance during project validation.

IEEE 802.3x refers to Ethernet flow control. It does not by itself establish traffic prioritization, deterministic timing or loss-free application delivery. Evaluate flow-control behaviour with the intended endpoints and traffic.

faqs.q: How should the DC supply be specified?
faqs.a: The reference lists 12, 24 and 48 V DC nominal supply values. Obtain the permitted input-voltage range, wiring schedule, input-circuit arrangement, consumption and protection details for the supplied version. The three nominal values alone do not define a continuous voltage range or a number of independent power inputs.

faqs.q: What does the -40 to +75 °C range apply to?
faqs.a: It is the operating-temperature range given for the switch reference. Check the conditions at the installation position inside the enclosure, including local heat sources and cooling. Confirm the applicable environmental and test conditions for the ordered configuration.

faqs.q: Are management functions, PoE or fibre ports included?
faqs.a: The documented HT7008 reference covers eight copper data ports. Specify any management, powered-device supply or fibre-connection requirement in the project brief. The written configuration proposal will identify the hardware and functions included in the ordered version.

faqs.q: Does redundant power also provide a redundant network?
faqs.a: Power-source arrangements and network-path resilience are separate design decisions. Agree the actual power-input circuits and transfer behaviour, then specify any network-recovery requirement independently. Do not create a loop without the required documented network functions.

faqs.q: Can the switch connect PLC, HMI and video equipment?
faqs.a: Compatible Ethernet endpoints can be included in the project port schedule. The endpoints still define their protocols and applications. Validate the traffic profile and any timing requirements; the switch reference does not establish protocol conversion or a safety-control function.

faqs.q: Can it be used outdoors, on ships or in hazardous areas?
faqs.a: Assess the complete installation against its enclosure, temperature, moisture, corrosion and regulatory requirements. The application examples are project contexts, not claims of outdoor ingress protection, marine approval, explosion protection or utility-sector certification. Obtain the required model-specific evidence before selection.

faqs.q: How does it fit into remote monitoring?
faqs.a: The switch connects local Ethernet equipment. Remote access and monitoring services depend on the connected router or gateway, endpoint software, receiving platform and project security design. Define that complete data path during integration; no built-in cellular or cloud-monitoring service is specified here.

faqs.q: What should an industrial switch customization brief include?
faqs.a: Provide the endpoint and port list, upstream network arrangement, traffic and timing needs, supply details, enclosure conditions, mounting constraints and destination requirements. Add requested network functions, product identification and documentation needs so the proposal can define the development, verification and delivery scope.
